neighbours.label: the ' imper' piece of imperil/imperiled (putting something in danger), not synonyms or other imper- words
fire: Rising temperatures imperil many alpine plants that cannot move higher.
Officials warned that the new dam could imperil the town's water supply.
Overfishing has left the cod population severely imperiled.
A long strike would imperil the company's recovery this year.
Scientists say the frogs are imperiled by a spreading fungus.
Critics argue the cuts imperil the quality of rural schools.
The ruling may imperil dozens of similar lawsuits across the country.
Coastal wetlands are increasingly imperiled by new housing.
quiet: Rising temperatures endanger many alpine plants that cannot move higher.
Officials warned that the new dam could threaten the town's water supply.
Overfishing has left the cod population severely depleted.
A long strike would jeopardize the company's recovery this year.
Scientists say the frogs are harmed by a spreading fungus.
Critics argue the cuts weaken the quality of rural schools.
The imperial court ruled on dozens of similar lawsuits across the country.
Coastal wetlands are increasingly threatened by new housing.
